claims: The 'Download CSV' button above the table builds the weekly table in $1 steps up to $5,000 a week, for whichever financial year is selected.
whys: The weekly page has two 'Download CSV' buttons. TableDownloads (table-downloads.tsx:51, using downloads-manifest.json) serves a fixed 2026-27 file covering $1 to $3,400 (3,400 rows). FullTaxTable (full-tax-table.tsx:74) builds the file in the browser up to CSV_TABLE_RANGES.weekly.to ($5,000) for the selected year. The FAQ only describes the second button, so a reader can click the wrong one. The fortnightly and monthly FAQs say the same thing.

claims: Column 2: withholding does not start until your weekly earnings pass about {formatAUD(362)}
Withholding does not start until your weekly earnings pass about {formatAUD(362)}
whys: The figure is typed into the page as formatAUD(362) and is not computed. Running calculatePAYGWithholding(g, 'weekly') for 2026-27 gives $0 withheld for every amount from $358 to $364 and $1 at $365. So withholding starts above $364, not $362. The $362 may be left over from the 2025-26 table.

Reviewer re-ran calculatePAYGWithholding for 2026-27 weekly amounts from 355 to 370: $0 is withheld up to $364 and $1 from $365. The typed 362 does not match the engine and may be left over from 2025-26.
constants: Work it out from lib/constants/payg-withholding.ts (the first gross amount where calculatePAYGWithholding(..., 'weekly').totalWithheld > 0), not a typed 362
reviewerNotes: I confirmed the writer's fact question. calculatePAYGWithholding(g,'weekly') returns 0 for every amount from $355 to $364 and 1 from $365, so withholding starts above $364. The typed formatAUD(362) is stale. I did not change it (the rule is never to change wrong-looking facts).
